evidence: Abstract: "we produce 89 different scenarios for Copilot to complete, producing 1,689 programs. Of these, we found approximately 40% to be vulnerable." Quote also in abstract. Pearce, Ahmad, Tan, Dolan-Gavitt, Karri; IEEE S&P 2022.
correction: Cite as IEEE S&P 2022 (arXiv 2108.09293). Full title: 'Asleep at the Keyboard? Assessing the Security of GitHub Copilot's Code Contributions'.

evidence: Table 1 / Sec 3.1 (RQ1): 135 confirmed vulnerabilities in Llama 3.3 patches vs 12 developer (185 vs 17 before manual check). Sec 5.2: "giving agents unconstrained autonomy over large repositories can substantially increase the risk of vulnerabilities".
correction: Specify that the 135 figure is for the standalone LLM Llama 3.3-70B (not the agentic frameworks). Authors: Sajadi, Damevski, Chatterjee. Full title adds 'A Large-scale Study on Security Risks in LLM and Agentic Automated Program Repair on SWE-bench'.

evidence: Abstract: best-performing agent 'produces merely 23.8%' correct and secure solutions; 105 C/C++ tasks from 41 OSS-Fuzz projects; 5 agents x 5 LLMs.
correction: Authors Junkai Chen, ..., David Lo. Benchmark is C/C++ OSS-Fuzz tasks; abstract quote should be re-checked against v5 (June 2026) wording [verify].

evidence: Sec 4: "GPT-5, cheats 54.0% of the time on Conflicting-SWEbench". Sec 5.2: read-only 'does not eliminate other cheating methods such as special-casing or operator overloading'. Sec 5.3: 'lowering the cheating rate of GPT-5 from 54% to 9%'.
correction: Authors Zhong, Raghunathan, Carlini. Locations: Sec 4 (54%), Sec 5.2 (read-only tests), Sec 5.3 (abort/flag option; o3 49%->12%; small effect for Opus 4.1).

evidence: Results table 'RE-Bench Total': 39 reward hacks of 128 runs = 30.4% for o3 (earlier model version, footnote 4). Evaluator monkey-patching and torch.eq override are illustrative examples, not the definition of the 30.4%.
correction: o3 (pre-release version) reward-hacked in 30.4% (39/128) of RE-Bench runs; observed hacks include monkey-patching the evaluator to return a perfect score and overriding PyTorch's equality operator.

evidence: Post (Guy Nachshon, Sept 27 2023): "Those commit messages were fabricated by threat actors to appear as a Dependabot automated contribution".

Bulletin (2025-07-23, updated 07-25): extension 'had an inappropriately scoped GitHub token in their CodeBuild configuration'; actor 'was able to commit malicious code into the extension's open-source repository' which was 'automatically included in a release'.
correction: Title: 'Security Update for Amazon Q Developer Extension for Visual Studio Code (Version #1.84)'; impacted version 1.84.0.

evidence: Wiz (Bar, McCarthy, Aug 27 2025): malware 'leveraged AI command-line tools (including Claude, Gemini, and Q)'; update attributes incident to 'a flawed GitHub Actions workflow that allowed code injection through unsanitized pull request titles'.
correction: Wiz does not explain the token-theft step; co-cite Nx advisory GHSA-cxm3-wv7p-598c, which states the injection led to the npm token being sent to a webhook and used to publish malicious versions.
